text.p: Arnold Palmer, who won seven major championships and lifted golf's popularity to unprecedented heights four decades ago, will undergo surgery Wednesday for treatment of prostate cancer.

The announcement was made Tuesday at the Mayo Medical Centre in Rochester, Minnesota, where Palmer just completed two days of testing. Palmer will remain hospitalized for several days following the procedure and will continue recuperating on an outpatient basis, medical centre officials announced.

The 67-year-old Palmer announced Friday that he was diagnosed with prostate cancer after undergoing a biopsy the day before. He withdrew from this week's Bob Hope Classic and said he doubts he will be play golf "until this thing is taken care of."
Prostate cancer is a slow-developing cancer that can be successfully treated if detected early.

Palmer, one of the most recognisable athletes in sports over the last four decades, won four Masters titles, two British Opens and one U.S. Open in his legendary career. He ranks fourth on the all-time PGA Tour victory list with 60 titles and has also won 10 Senior Tournaments.
His charismatic come-from-behind charges in the 1960s developed a loyal following that earned the nickname "Arnie's Army."
